About Lectroni
Lectroni is the parent company behind a portfolio of operating brands across automotive, lubricants, and industrial markets. About the eBay Store
The Lectroni eBay store has operated since 2014 and carries an established trading history with strong feedback. Its product range spans tyres, oils, heaters, and equipment — effectively every category we hold inventory in. The current limitation is not reputation or reach but cadence: listings are not refreshed often enough, and merchandising is inconsistent. Tightening the operating rhythm should produce meaningful revenue gains without new acquisition spend.

The Eiffel Shop is our direct-to-customer storefront, operating alongside our eBay listings. About Amaze Heaters
Amaze is a newly launched range of slim convection wall panel heaters. The product is differentiated on three dimensions that matter to specific buyer segments: silent operation, paintable surface that allows it to integrate with interior design, and low power draw that makes it suitable for home battery systems and caravans — categories where most conventional heaters cannot operate. As the most recent addition to the portfolio it has the highest growth ceiling and requires the most investment in brand-building from a near-zero base.
Background — who and whyclick to expand

Who Buys Amaze

  • Homeowners and renovators wanting a stylish heater
  • Caravan and RV owners needing low-power heating
  • Builders, electricians, property developers
  • Aged care and disability sector — silent, no burns risk
  • Hospitality and commercial buildings

What Makes Amaze Special

  • 100% silent — no fans, no moving parts
  • Ultra-slim and paintable — looks like part of the wall
  • Low power draw — runs on home batteries and caravan outlets
  • Convection heat — soft warmth, not blasting hot air
  • Australian-tested and safe

About HACOclick to expand
About HACO
HACO is an independent not-for-profit retailer selling consumable goods — primarily honey, dates, and biodegradable tableware — with all profits directed to community programs. The structural difference from a traditional charity is that HACO funds itself through commerce rather than through donations. The longer-term ambition is to scale this into Australia's most profitable not-for-profit and, eventually, a cooperative network of physical stores. Lectroni provides operational infrastructure at no cost so HACO can direct every dollar of profit to its programs.
Background — who and whyclick to expand

Who Buys From HACO

  • Diaspora and ethnic community members
  • The wider Australian public who want to support a cause
  • Anyone who values giving back through purchasing

  • Number of unique supporters and buyers
  • Repeat purchase rate (loyalty signal)
  • Cost per dollar funded — efficiency matters
  • Volunteer / ambassador growth

About TBL Online Orderingclick to expand
About TBL Online Ordering
TBL is the trade ordering platform used by our regular B2B customers — workshops, fleets, and resellers — to place repeat orders directly. It replaces the slower phone and email ordering process with a saved-favourites checkout that takes most customers under a minute. The strategic value compounds with usage: once a customer has built up their saved order history within the platform, the cost of switching to another supplier increases substantially. This makes TBL both an operational efficiency tool and a long-term retention mechanism.
Background — who and whyclick to expand

Who Uses TBL

  • Workshops and mechanics placing regular orders
  • Fleet operators ordering for vehicle servicing
  • Trade customers who already know us
  • Not open to public — invitation only

Why TBL Matters

  • Saves us time — no more "what was that order?" calls
  • Saves them time — re-ordering becomes a 30-second job
  • Reduces order errors versus manual entry
  • Locks in customer loyalty through saved orders and pricing

Torqd App

CarFax for truck tyres. The biggest opportunity we have built.
Torqd is built and owned by Lectroni. It records every truck tyre fitment so fleets and fitters can prove what was done, track performance, and calculate cost per kilometre. Long-term, this could become a standalone software business.
The strategic opportunity. The real prize is not subscription revenue — it's the data. Tyre manufacturers will eventually pay for the analytics and insights this app generates.

About Torqdclick to expand
About Torqd
Torqd is a SaaS platform that records every truck-tyre fitment performed by participating fitters and fleets, capturing tyre brand, axle position, vehicle, mileage, and outcome. The current Australian market has no systematic record of this data — fitters complete the work, fleets pay the invoice, and the operational history is lost. Torqd captures that history and over time produces a structured dataset on tyre performance, fitter quality, and fleet behaviour. The long-term commercial opportunity sits less in subscription revenue than in the analytical value of the dataset to tyre manufacturers, insurers, and fleet operators.
Background — who and whyclick to expand

Who Uses Torqd Today

  • Mobile truck tyre fitters — record each fitment
  • Fleet managers — see cost-per-km and tyre performance
  • Insurance and warranty processors — verify what was fitted
  • Future: tyre manufacturers will pay for the data and insights

How Torqd Will Make Money

  • Today: Free for all users — building user base
  • Soon: Subscriptions from fitters and fleets
  • The big prize: Tyre manufacturers paying for data, insights, and advertising

Your Job for This Asset

This asset has specialised needs — some work may need Australian on-the-ground execution.

  • Recruit beta fitters in target freight corridors — relationship-driven, not broad outreach
  • Manage industry presence — content for trucking forums, Facebook groups, transport magazines
  • App Store Optimisation — niche keywords, not broad SEO
  • Coordinate trade show and association engagement (Australian Trucking Association)
  • Account-based outreach to top 50 freight companies and top 100 mobile fitters
  • Track fitter retention metrics — week 1, week 4, week 12 — flag drop-offs
  • Begin manufacturer relationship groundwork — track conversations, share research

📍 Hosting at ops.lectroni.com.au

This dashboard is designed to be uploaded to ops.lectroni.com.au as a single HTML file. To deploy: simply upload this file to your web host and point the subdomain to it.

Important about data sync: Each browser stores its own copy of the data locally. To share updates between you and your offshore team, use the Export button (top-right) to save a JSON file, send it via email or shared drive, and have the recipient use Import to load it.

Manage Digital Assets

Add, edit, or remove the digital properties you're tracking.

Asset Logos

Upload a logo for each asset. PNG with transparent background works best. Max ~2MB per file.

Recurring Task Templates

Routine tasks that auto-generate. The system creates these automatically — when you open the dashboard, any due recurring tasks for today will be added if they don't exist yet.

Data Management

All data is stored in your browser. Use Export to back up or share with your team member, Import to restore.

How to Use This Dashboard

Manager workflow. Each morning, review yesterday's Daily Log, check Dashboard for overdue/critical tasks. Assign new tasks with hour estimates. Once a month: set budgets, review the Performance tab to see ROI.

Team workflow. Open dashboard each morning. Sort by priority. Move tasks: To Do → In Progress → Review → Done. Always log actual hours and paste a proof URL when marking done. Post Daily Log at end of day. Each Friday: log this week's ad spend in the Budgets tab.

Budget rhythm. Set monthly budgets at start of month. Team logs ad spend every Friday. Review Performance tab around the 3rd of each new month once previous month's KPIs are entered.

Sharing data. Either work from the same hosted URL (upload to Google Drive/Dropbox shared folder, or your website), or use Export/Import to sync — team exports at end of week, emails JSON to you, you import on Monday.

Manage channels for

Channels are the digital surfaces this asset shows up on — websites, social pages, marketplace listings, app stores. Mark each as Live (we're running it), Planned (need to build), Dormant (account exists, not active), or Archived (closed). Add a URL if you have one.
